findings.title: test_dedupe expected occurrence is built with wrong group_key, breaking equality assertion
findings.body: In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe, build_mock_occurrence_and_event is called with group_key='val1' and value=6 to populate the expected_result, but evaluate_group_key_value is then invoked with expected_result.group_key ('group_key') and value=10. Because build_mock_occurrence_and_event sets fingerprint via handler.build_fingerprint(group_key), the expected IssueOccurrence gets fingerprint [f'{detector_id}:val1'] while the one produced inside evaluate_group_key_value (via build_occurrence_and_event_data -> build_mock_occurrence_and_event) gets [f'{detector_id}:group_key']. IssueOccurrence is constructed positionally as a dataclass, so the fingerprints are part of __eq__; the assertion comparing the result to expected_result will fail. The call should be build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, 'group_key', 10, PriorityLevel.HIGH) so the expected and actual occurrences match. The same copy/paste-style hardcoding of 'val1'/6 also appears in other tests in this file (e.g. test_results_on_change) where it happens to be harmless because the evaluate call uses 'val1' too, but it is fragile.

findings.title: get_state_data raises KeyError when counter_names is empty
findings.body: In StatefulDetectorHandler.get_state_data, when self.counter_names is an empty list the 'if self.counter_names:' block is skipped, leaving counter_updates = {}. The subsequent loop then executes 'counter_updates=counter_updates[gk]' on this empty dict, which raises KeyError for every group_key. Since counter_names is declared as an abstract list[str] property and a handler is permitted to legitimately return [] (no counters to track), this is a real latent bug. The fix is to initialize counter_updates to {gk: {} for gk in group_keys} before the if block (or to default to {} inside the DetectorStateData construction when no counter data is available).

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler cannot be instantiated: abstract methods unimplemented
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is defined as 'class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass' but StatefulDetectorHandler declares several @abc.abstractmethod methods that it does not implement: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly-added build_occurrence_and_event_data. Calling MetricAlertDetectorHandler(detector) will raise TypeError. The TODO comment marks this as deliberate placeholder work, but the class is still exported (referenced from MetricAlertFire.detector_handler) so any caller that triggers detector.detector_handler on a MetricAlertFire GroupType will crash with a non-obvious TypeError rather than a clear 'not implemented' error. Consider either raising NotImplementedError in a custom __init__/__new__ or wiring this through a registry entry that is left unset until the abstraction is implemented.
